{{Short description|Upper bound on the volume of a convex body containing one lattice point}}

[[File:Ehrhart conjecture.svg|thumb|A standard simplex in <math>n = 2</math> dimensions, scaled by <math>n+1 = 3</math>, with <math>(1, 1)</math> at its [[barycenter]]. Equality is achieved, with the area being <math>(n+1)^n/n! = 9/2</math>]]

In the [[geometry of numbers]], '''Ehrhart's volume conjecture''' gives an upper bound on the volume of a [[convex body]] containing only one [[integer lattice|lattice point]] in its interior.  It is a kind of converse to [[Minkowski's theorem]], which guarantees that a centrally symmetric convex body <math>K</math> must contain a lattice point as soon as its volume exceeds <math>2^n</math>.  The conjecture states that a convex body <math>K</math> containing only one lattice point in its interior as its [[Center_of_mass|barycenter]] cannot have volume greater than <math>(n+1)^n/n!</math>:
:<math>\operatorname{Vol}(K) \le \frac{(n+1)^n}{n!}.</math>
Equality is achieved in this inequality when <math>K=(n+1)\Delta_n</math> is a copy of the [[standard simplex]] in Euclidean <math>n</math>-dimensional space, whose sides are scaled up by a factor of <math>n+1</math>.  Equivalently, <math>K=(n+1)\Delta_n</math> is congruent to the convex hull of the vectors <math>-\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf{e}_i</math>, and <math>(n+1)\mathbf{e}_j - \sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf{e}_i </math> for all <math> j=1,\ldots,n </math>.  Presented in this manner, the origin is the only lattice point interior to the convex body <math>K</math>.

The conjecture, furthermore, asserts that equality is achieved in the above inequality if and only if <math>K</math> is unimodularly equivalent to <math>(n+1)\Delta_n</math>.

== History and resolution ==

[[Eugene Ehrhart]] proved the conjecture in [[dimension]] 2 and in the special case of [[simplex|simplices]] in arbitrary dimensions.{{sfn|Ehrhart|1967}} For several decades, the general conjecture remained open despite efforts by numerous mathematicians.

In 2014, Benjamin Nill and Andreas Paffenholz confirmed the conjecture for several important classes of rational [[polytope]]s, establishing that equality holds if and only if <math>K</math> is unimodularly equivalent to the standard simplex.{{sfn|Nill|Paffenholz|2014}}

In August 2026, [[OpenAI]] announced that its Astra reasoning model proved the inequality part of the conjecture, establishing the sharp upper bound <math>\operatorname{Vol}(K) \le (n+1)^n/n!</math>, with the proof formally verified in [[Lean (proof assistant)|Lean 4]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-08-01 |title=Ten advances in mathematics and theoretical computer science |url=https://openai.com/index/ten-advances-in-mathematics/ |access-date=2026-08-04 |website=OpenAI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="OpenAI-report">{{Cite report |author=OpenAI |date=2026-08-01 |title=Ten Advances in Mathematics and Theoretical Computer Science |url=https://cdn.openai.com/pdf/ten-proofs-oai.pdf |pages=217–218 |access-date=2026-08-04}}</ref><ref name="ten-proofs">{{cite web |title=ten-proofs: Formal proofs for ten open problems |url=https://github.com/openai/ten-proofs |website=GitHub |access-date=7 September 2026}}</ref>{{secondary source needed|date=September 2026}}
